Theme 082 · Characters & mascots

Kaomoji Terminal

The whole film lives in a terminal, and Pulse’s only body is a kaomoji — a face made of type. It dozes (-_-), watches (•_•), gasps (°o°;) and relaxes (^_^)b while the log stream scrolls; the human answers the prompt with one keystroke.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Kaomoji face — Pulse’s entire body: 4 expressions built from ASCII
  • Log stream — timestamped metric lines in mono; ok in green
  • Hot line — the anomaly row: coral bar, tinted background
  • Prompt box — the question + [R] roll back / [A] acknowledge keys
  • Human input — ‘you> R’ with a blinking block cursor
  • Terminal chrome — minimal window bar + faint scanlines

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Type-on — characters at 20 chars/s, 1 line per 8th note in logs; punctuation pauses snap to the next beat (120 BPM grid)
  • Face swap — hard cut between kaomoji on quarter notes, with a 1-frame scale 1.08 pop — never tweened
  • Cursor blink — block cursor 0.25 s on / 0.25 s off (8ths), holding solid while the human types

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: Nothing is cheaper to produce and nothing is more native for developer tools: type is the character, emotion reads instantly from a kaomoji, and the prompt makes the human decision explicit. Risk: Terminal aesthetics exclude non-technical buyers and dense logs are hard to read at feed size; keep only 5 log lines and one giant face per frame.

Adapt to your product: Replace the log lines with your own CLI or event stream, pick 4 kaomoji for your idle/watching/alert/done states, and turn your primary action into a single-key prompt.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaomoji (Japanese text faces read upright, emphasising the eyes) · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emoticon (the 1982 origin of text faces in plain-text messaging)
